- [2023/05/24] The appellant argued that they were not responsible for the installation of flashing around windows due to specific contractual terms.
- [2023/05/24] The respondents claimed that the contract terms were superseded by a Deed, specifically clause 14, which constituted the entire agreement.
- [2023/05/24] The appellant referred to clause 7 of the Deed, arguing it preserved the terms of the original contract.
- [2023/05/24] The Tribunal preferred the expert evidence of Mr. Brennan over Mr. Sim regarding the necessity of flashing for windows.
- [2023/05/24] Mr. Brennan's report indicated that the absence of flashing and small joint sealer caused window leaks.
- [2023/05/24] Mr. Sim argued that additional flashing was unnecessary due to the use of commercial-grade sections and sub-heads/sills.
- [2023/05/24] The Tribunal concluded that the windows required flashing and were defective due to the absence of small joint sealant.
- [2023/05/24] The Tribunal rejected the appellant's submission that the builder was responsible for flashing, determining the windows were defective regardless of flashing responsibility.
- [2023/05/24] The Tribunal found that the absence of flashing contributed to leakage but did not alter the conclusion of window defectiveness.
